q: What does a priority queue give you that a plain queue does not?
options: The best item (for example the smallest) comes out first, not the oldest
Items stay sorted at all times
Any item can be read in O(1)
why: A shop line serves the oldest first. An emergency room sees the most urgent first.

q: What is the rule of a min-heap?
options: Every parent is smaller than or equal to its children
The left child is always smaller than the right child
Every child is bigger than all items above it
why: Only the top is known to be the smallest. A heap is not sorted.

q: In the array form of a heap, where are the children of index `i`?
why: The parent of `i` is `(i - 1) >> 1`. A full tree fits in an array with no pointers.

q: What do push and pop cost in a heap?
why: Each one walks one path of about log n levels: bubble up after push, sink down after pop.

q: To find the k BIGGEST numbers, why keep a MIN-heap of size k?
options: Its top is the smallest of the k best, the one a new number must beat
A max-heap cannot hold k items
The biggest numbers sink to the bottom of a min-heap
why: A new number only has to beat the weakest of the current best k. That is exactly the top.

q: Top 10 of 1,000,000 numbers: heap of size 10 against sorting everything. What did I measure?
options: The heap took about 14 to 25 ms, the sort about 200 to 250 ms
The heap ran out of memory
why: The heap is O(n log k) and the sort is O(n log n). With a small k it is about 10 times faster here.
